steps.title: Identify Study Population
steps.instruction: Retrieve a list of households and elderly persons (aged 65 years and above) residing in locations represented by a Community Health Unit (CHU) from existing household health records held by Community Health Workers (CHW).

steps.title: Select Households for Interview
steps.instruction: Use systematic random sampling to select households for interviews.

substeps.instruction: Select the first household using simple random sampling from the first fifteen households in the area.
Move in one direction systematically starting from the main street of the study area to identify subsequent households.

steps.title: Screen and Select Participants
steps.instruction: Apply inclusion and exclusion criteria to residents of Gatanga Sub-county for the last 1 year.

substeps.instruction: Exclude elderly persons with physical disabilities limiting the use of both feet for walking and arms for support that occurred before the preceding one year.

Exclude those unable to provide information due to severe mental incapacitation, assessed by orientation to time, place, and person, and ability to perform activities of daily living (self-feeding, self-bathroom care, self-grooming, and normal interaction).
If multiple eligible members exist in a household, toss a one-shilling coin (Heads = Male, Tails = Female) to select the interviewee.
If an eligible member is absent, revisit at a later time or date; if no eligible member exists, select the next household on the sampling list.

steps.title: Conduct Structured Interviews
steps.instruction: Administer structured interview forms to the selected participants (target sample size of 424, accounting for 10% non-response) between September 4th and 15th, 2017.

substeps.instruction: Collect data on the main outcome variable: reported falls in the preceding year (September 2016 to August 2017), defined as sudden unintentional coming to rest from level ground, excluding falls from heights, vehicles, or aggressive pushes by farm animals.
Collect fall details: number of events, time and place of last fall, presence of companions, and immediate circumstances leading to the fall.
Record complications: immobilization, fear of falling, abandonment of daily activities, loss of autonomy, hospitalization, skin bruises, fractures, head injury, and confusion.
Collect socio-demographic data: age, gender, marital status, and education level.

Collect medical data: current medication, alcohol/cigarette use, active treatment for diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, kidney disease, joint pains (ankle, knees, hip, fingers, wrist, elbow, shoulder), lower back pains, recurrent syncope, cancer, stroke, anemia, depressed mood, acute stress, headache, peripheral neuropathy, wounds, pressure sores, bruises, cuts, acute illnesses, and altered mental states.
Investigate foot problems: foot pains and jigger infestation.
Assess frailty using the Frailty for Non-Disabled (FiND) index questionnaire, unsteadiness in gait/balance, and difficulty in usual activities.
Evaluate nutrition status using the Mini Nutrition Assessment – Short Form (MNA-SF).
Assess functional capacity using a Modified Barthel Index of activities of daily living.

Investigate socio-economic/environmental factors: residential floor type, night lighting source, living arrangements (alone or with others), daily activity involvement, attendance to domestic animals, and source of healthcare funds.

steps.title: Validate Data
steps.instruction: Mitigate recall bias by sourcing collaborative history and verifying medical records.

substeps.instruction: Request participants to provide current medications and hospital records (prescriptions, visit cards).
Source collaborative information from close family members and contacts to ascertain treatment history.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Convert hard copy data to soft copy using Epi Info version 3.5.4 and analyze using STATA 13.0.

substeps.instruction: Compute descriptive statistics (mean, mode, median with 95% confidence intervals) for age, sex, medical conditions, and lifestyle factors.
Perform bivariate analysis using Pearson’s Chi-square to establish associations between factors and falls.
Perform multivariate analysis using a logistic regression model to identify significantly associated factors.

description: For significance testing in bivariate analysis, Pearson’s Chi Square Test was used for categorical variables and p<0.05 was considered statistically significant (47). Subsequently, those variables statistically significant (𝑃-value <0.10) in the bivariate analysis were entered into a logistic regression model to evaluate the independent associations between falls and characteristics of the participants. Results of the regression model were presented as odds ratios (OR) with their 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) (48).
